question: Which of the following is NOT used as food preservative?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium hydrogen carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sodium hydrogen carbonate** is also known as baking soda.
 
• Baking soda is primarily used as a leavening agent in baking, not as a food preservative.
 
• **Preservatives** such as sodium benzoate, table salt, and sugar are commonly used to prevent spoilage and extend shelf life of food products.
 
• Sodium hydrogen carbonate is used in cooking for its **ability to produce carbon dioxide gas** when heated or combined with an acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Food Preservatives:**

 
 
• Substances added to food to prevent spoilage caused by microorganisms, enzymes, and oxidation.
 
• Examples include sodium benzoate, nitrates, sulfites, and sorbic acid.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Benzoate:**
 
 
• A widely used food preservative that inhibits the growth of mold, yeast, and some bacteria.
 
• Commonly used in acidic foods like salad dressings, carbonated drinks, and fruit juices.
 
 
 
• **Table Salt (Sodium Chloride):**
 
 
• One of the oldest and most common food preservatives.
 
• Works by drawing moisture out of food, inhibiting the growth of bacteria and mold.
 
 
 
• **Sugar:**
 
 
• Used as a preservative in jams, jellies, and syrups.
 
• Preserves food by reducing the water activity, thus inhibiting microbial growth.
